source: NASA Apollo 11 Technical Air-to-Ground and Onboard Voice Transcriptions, via Spacelog (spacelog.org)
lines: And, Houston, Eagle here. Both RCS helium pressures are reading 2900. Over.
Roger, Buzz. There seems to be some confusion here on 405 and 406. We'd like you to zero them out prior to undocking, and after undocking you can - we'd like them still zeroed. Over.
Roger. I agree with that. Thank you.
Eagle, Houston. We've got the load in the - We have reselected P00; your integration is going again for you; the computer is yours. We'd like to do the drift check now. Over.
Columbia, let's flick it in 0620 when you are ready.
Standing by until your Mark, Neil.
Eagle, Houston. We've copied the angles and will read back if you are ready. Over.
That's correct, and GET was 99 hours and 4 minutes even.
Eagle, Houston. Have you initialized the AGS yet? Over.
Negative. I haven't had a state vector yet.
Roger, Buzz. Have you done the 377 yet?
Roger. Standing by for your K factor.
Columbia, Houston. We have got a load for you. Could we have P00 and ACCEPT? Over.
Roger. Thank you, Mike. And break. Eagle, we've got a K factor for you. Over.
Roger, Buzz. K factor coming at you: 90 00 00 15. Over.
Roger. That's good. That's a good ENTER there.
Eagle, Houston. We recommend the AGS initial - Well, we see it coming up now on the AGS initialization. Over.
Eagle, Houston. After the AGS initialization, we'll be ready for the RCS checkout.
Columbia, Houston. We got the load in. You can go back to BLOCK.
Columbia, Houston. Did you get a - copy any LM data, low bit rate, behind the Moon? Over.
Or at least I've configured for it. I'm not sure Eagle sent it or not.
No, we did not send V data. Eagle. Over.
Eagle, Houston. The alignment and the initialization looked good to us. Over.
Apollo 11, Houston. LOS is 99 30; next AOS 100 16. Over.
Eagle, Columbia. Let me know when you come to your RCS hot fire checks so I can disable my roll.
Roger. We're right there now. And we'd like you - CSM in MID deadband ATT hold. Over.
And, Houston, you have high bit rate with us now, I believe? We're ready to proceed with the RCS checks.
Roger, Eagle. We're standing by. We're ready. Over.
Columbia, we'd like wide deadband ATT hold. Over.
Okay. Going wide deadband ATT hold.
Are you going to do your hot fire now?
Roger. Would you believe you've got thrusters on board that vehicle.
Give me a call just as soon as your hot fire is complete, please.
Houston, Eagle. The RCS hot fire is complete. How did you observe it? Over.
Stand by. Eagle, Houston. The RCS hot fire looks super to us. We're all GO.
Roger. Mike, would you confirm that thrusters B3 and C4 are off? Over. And your radar transponder off.
C4 is off; B3 is off. Transponder is to HEATER which is the same as being off, and I've got my roll jets back on now.
Apollo 11, Houston. We're GO for undocking. Over.
Starting a trim maneuver to AGS CAL attitude.
Roger. There will be no television of the undocking. I have all available windows either full of heads or cameras, and I'm busy with other things.
And, Eagle, Houston. We'd like you to select aft OMNI now. It will be good for both LOS and AOS. Over.
Apollo 11, Houston. One minute to LOS.
It's nice and quiet over here, isn't it?
Okay, everything's going well. Everything's quiet over on this side.
Okay. I'm standing by to record your data anytime it's convenient for you; angles coming up in another 2 minutes.
Okay, I'm ready to go to B DATA now.
Columbia, Eagle. How do you read?
Read you loud and clear, Buzz.
Mike, are you in AGS CAL attitude now?

That's affirm. I'm holding you there with the DAP, getting the deadband. When you get ready to do the AGS CAL, I will sort of quiet down the thruster firing and then hope to stop it altogether, but I don't even think that'll get it.
Okay. Well, I'm just about ready to do that. Whenever you're ready to let it go free, why just tell me.
Okay, it looks real quiet now; I'm ready to go right now.
Now, ... might check me on this, I - it's - I'm ready to go anytime you're ready.
Roger. We'll be ready to go in just a minute.
Okay, I'm starting my 5-minute rate - right now.
As a matter of interest, I appear to be drifting in my roll; I'm holding my pitch and yaw pretty constant, and I'm staying a good 15 degrees late in the program.
Halfway through it, it looks like I have ... degrees in roll is about all.
Yes, those look like good ones right now.
GET of the separation burn is 100:39:50 even.
I haven't gotten the updates for undocking time; I'm still carrying 100 hours 15 minutes, I guess, ...
I'm surprised they didn't update it by 3 or 4 minutes to, you know, make that DELTA-V be in the same position that they wanted.
So we're about 3 minutes ahead of the printed flight plan; it might be wise to try to SEP about 3 minutes early, and we can give them a GET of SEP that's precise whenever they want it.
I have 5 minutes and 15 seconds since we started. Attitude is holding very well.
Roger, Mike. Just hold it a little bit longer.
No sweat, I can hold it all day. Take your sweet time. How's the Czar over there? He's so quiet.
I didn't know ... radio. ... I've ever seen a radio. All I can say is, "Beware the revolution."
You cats take it easy on the lunar surface; if I hear you huffing and puffing, I'm going to start bitching at you.
I just pressurized the DPS. ... looks okay, Mike.
Hey, Mike, can you see where our radar's pointing now?
Well, it looks like it's pointed right at my head; that's hard south; so's your radio beacon.
Okay. It should really - it should be pointing from the - you know, our forward axis? It should be pointing up at 40 degrees and, you know -
Okay. We've wandered back over the bellyband now - let me assure that AGS CAL.
How'd the AGS CAL work out?
Oh, it danced around a little bit, but seemed to go right back to the original numbers.
Okay. I'm going to start a maneuver now to our undocking attitude.

Now the undock attitude and the SEP attitude ought to be the same, so I'm going to go to what they gave me for the updated separation-burn attitude. That's just about 7 degrees off, but it's in your flight plan for the undock attitude.
When your rendezvous radar self-test is complete, let me know and I'll check out my transponder.
Excuse me, Mike, what did you say?
I say, when your rendezvous radar self-test is complete, let me know and I'll check out my transponder.
Yes, we're through with that now.
That transponder checked out. I hope they've got a nice, big, strong ... for you.
Hey, Mike, what would you recommend as a good setting on the 16 millimeter?

Well, what they recommend for you is f:8 at 1/250th and put it not on infinity, but on 7 feet, which covers all the way from infinity down to a very short distance to keep it in focus, and 6 frames per second, I guess.
Yes, what you say, f:8 at 1/250th?
Yes, f:8 at 1/250th. And after you get it all set up, check that f-stop again because it slides and slips off with very little twist.
How about using, as an undocking time, 100 hours and 12 minutes? That suit your fancy?
What have you got for AOS, Mike?
We got just about a minute to go; you guys all set?
Yes, I think we're about ready.
We're all set when you are, Mike.
Okay. I've killed my rate, Mike, so you drift out to the distance you like and then stop your rate.
There's sure a better visual in the simulator.
Okay. I picked up a little roll; I'm going to get rid of it.
Okay with you if I start my pitch, or you think you're not far enough away yet, Mike?
I'd prefer you stand by just a couple of seconds, Neil.
Okay. I'll wait for when you're ready – when you think you've got your rates killed perfectly.
Okay, looks pretty good to me now.
Just like in the simulator, you're drifting off to one side and down below a little bit.
Hello, Eagle. Houston. We're standing by. Over.
The gear are looking good; I've seen three of them.
The MESA is not down, right?
Eagle, Houston. We see you on the steerable. Over.
Roger. Eagle's undocked. The Eagle has wings. Looking good.
Roger. How does it look, Neil?
Roger, Neil. We got a - If you will give us P00 and DATA, we've got the loads for you.
Okay. You've got it, P00 and DATA.
Okay. You've got it. P00 and DATA.
Roger. Let us know when you are ready to copy. We have a DOI PAD, and a PDI PAD. Over.
You check our tracking light, Mike?
You check our tracking light, Mike?
Back off? Okay. I'm ready to start my yaw maneuver if it suits you, Mike.
I'm ready to start my yaw maneuver if it suits you, Mike.
Does it look like you're going to be able to do this without firing any thrusters, Mike?
Does it look like you are going to be able to do this without burning thrusters, Mike?
I'd have to fire laterally once or twice.
Go ahead, Houston. Eagle is ready to copy.
Go ahead, Houston. Eagle is ready to copy.

Roger, Eagle. Coming at you with a DOI PAD: 101 36 14.07. NOUN 81, minus 00758, plus all balls, plus 00098 plus - correction, 00572, perigee plus 00085 00764 030 000 293. Understand you are ready to copy the PDI data, Eagle. Over
That's affirmative. Go ahead with the PDI.
That's affirmative. Go ahead with the PDI.

Roger. PDI PAD: TIG 102 33 04.36 09 50, minus 00021, 182 287 000, plus 56919. PDI abort, less than 10 minutes, 105 12 30.00. PDI abort, greater than 10 minutes, 103 40 00.00 107 11 30.00. No PDI plus 12: 102 44 27.00. NOUN 81 plus 01223, minus all balls, plus 01889 01520 plus 00110 02250, burn time 046 000 190, plus 01187, plus all balls, plus 01911. NOUN 11 103 31 07.00. NOUN 37 105 12 30.00. Ready for your readbacks, Over.
Eagle, Houston. We are through with the computer. You can go, back to BLOCK. Over.
Roger. Back to BLOCK and DOI: 101:36:14.07; minus 0075.8, plus all zeros, plus 0009.8; 0057.2, plus 0008.5, 0076.4, 0:3O; 000, 293; minus 0075.9, plus all zeros, plus 0009.0; NA. Over.
Roger. Back to BLOCK; and REALIGN: 101 36 14.07 minus 00758,plus all zeros, plus 00098 00572, plus 00085 00764 030 000 293, minus 000759, plus all zeros, plus 00090. NA. Over.
That was a good readback, Buzz. Go ahead. Over.
Houston, Eagle. Are you copying the fairly large numbers for range and range rate in - VERB 83? And did you - you just give us a state vector that changed one of the two vehicles? Over.
Houston, Eagle. Are you copying the very large numbers for range and range rate in VERB 83? And did you just give us a state vector that changed one of the two vehicles? Over.
Roger, Eagle. We gave you a LM state vector. We have not changed the CSM state vector, however. Over.
Columbia, Houston. On my Mark 9 30 to ignition.
Eagle, Houston. Would you have Columbia go to the high gain, yaw 0, pitch minus 20. Over.
You want him to go to HIGH GAIN, YAW, zero or - say again the numbers.
You want him to go to high gain yaw 0? Say again the numbers.
Roger, Neil. Yaw 0, pitch minus 20, high gain angles. Over.
Okay. YAW, zero; PITCH, minus 20, on the HIGH GAIN. Columbia.
Okay. Yaw 0, pitch minus 20 on the high gain.
That's affirmative. We've lost all data with him.
Yes, I copy that, and I'll do it just as soon as I get to it.
Okay, he says he'll do that as soon as he gets around there.
He says he'll do that as soon as he gets around there.
Okay, Neil, I'm all set for the SEP burn, and we're looking good on this phasing.
Columbia, Houston. How do you read?
Columbia, read you loud and clear. Houston, how me?
I read you loud and clear, Houston. How me?
Roger, Mike. Five by. On my Mark 7 minutes to ignition.
I agree. Everything's looking real good.
Apollo 11, Houston. You are looking good for separation. You are GO for separation, Columbia. Over.
We're really stabilized, Neil. I haven't burned a thruster in 5 minutes.
I'll make a small trim maneuver.
Mike, what's going to be your pitch angle at SEP?
Is that close enough for you or do you want it to a couple of decimal places?
I think you've got a fine looking flying machine there, Eagle, despite the fact you're upside down.
Okay, Eagle. One minute until TIG. You guys take care.
Houston, Columbia. My DSKY is reading 4.9, in X, 5.0 ..., make it and EMS 105.4. Over.
Roger. Copy. Columbia, it looks good to us. Over.
Columbia, Houston. We'd like you to terminate average G. Over.
You're going right down U.S. 1, Mike.
Eagle, Columbia. At your convenience, I would like to switch over to VHF ranging modes.
Roger. Let's go to VHF ranging now.
Eagle, Columbia. I am reading you loud and scratchy. Neil is not coming through too well on his VOX. Could you be quiet for 15 seconds while I get this locked on.
I've got a solid lock on. I have you at 0.27 miles.
Eagle, Houston. We've got a state vector for you. We'd like P00 and DATA. Over.
Columbia, Houston. We have a CSM rescue PAD if you are ready to copy. Over.
Roger, Mike. Phasing TIG 103 40 0000, TPI for PDI less that 10, 105 12 3000, TPI for PDI greater than 10, 107 11 3000. Over.
Roger. TIG's follow: phasing 103 40, PDI less than 10, 105 12 30 more than 10, 107 11 30. Over.
Eagle, Houston. When you are ready to copy, I have a lunar surface data PAD for you. Over.
We've got the load in, Eagle. You can go back updata link OFF. Over.
Columbia, Houston. At your convenience we'd like P00 and ACCEPT. We have a couple of state vectors for you. Over.
Okay. Going to P00 and ACCEPT, and I just got some unexplained roll thruster activity. I might have bumped the hand controller.
Roger. We will look at it. Out
And Eagle is ready to copy lunar surface data PAD.

Roger, Buzz. Starting with the T2, T2 TIG: 102 54 2900 103 51 5600 106 37 3500 109 10 0000. In the remarks: T2 occurs at PDI plus 2126. T3 time - correction T3, T3 TIG: 104 39 4100 001 58 1500 001 58 5400. NOUN 11: 105 36 2300 107 11 3000. Ready for your readback. Over.

Mike, you want to give us a Mark when you're right at 7 miles - I mean seven tenths of a mile?
Okay. We just got seven tenths on the radar.
Yes. I'm oscillating between 0.69 and seven tenths.
Very good. We've got 4200 on the ... meter.
I'm steady on 70 now. Yes. I read you sort of scratchy, but I read you.
Houston, Apollo - or Houston, Columbia. Over.
Roger. I still need a DOI P76 PAD, and a PDI 1 plus 12 P76 PAD sometime at your convenience.
Columbia, Houston. DOI P76 PAD, if you're ready to copy. Over.
Roger, Mike. NOUN 80 - correction, NOUN 84: minus 00758, plus all zeros, plus 00098; NOUN 33: 101 36 1400, and stand by for the PDI plus 12.
Columbia, Houston, with the PDI plus 12 NOUN 84, if you're ready to copy.
Roger. NOUN 84: plus 01223, minus all zeros, plus 01889; NOUN 33: 102 44 2700, PDI plus 12 burn time is 046, burn time for DOI is 030. Ready for your readback. Over.
Roger. DOI P76: 84 is minus 00758, all balls, plus 00098, at 101 36 1400; plus 01223, minus all balls, plus 01889, 102 44 2700; burn time 46 and 30 seconds.
Roger. One error, Columbia, on the TIG for DOI; seconds was 1407. Over.
Columbia, Houston. We'd like you to turn off your rotational direct - rotational control power direct number 2 off. Over.
Columbia, Houston. On those P76's, a friendly reminder from your FIDO: add half the burn time to the TIG. Over.
Columbia, Houston. We've lost data with Eagle. Will you please have him select aft OMNI? Over.
Eagle, this is Columbia. Houston would like you to select aft OMNI.
Roger. I got it now. Houston, you reading Eagle now on aft OMNI?
That's affirmative, Eagle. Reading you five by.
Columbia, Houston. We'll have LOS at 101 28. AOS for you 102 15. Over.
Eagle, Houston. It appeared to us when you were doing the P52, maneuvering the S band, the high gain went into the stop. Verify that both S band breakers are in. Over.
Roger. I think I'd gone up to 90.0 before it went there. The one on this side is in and I'll check the other later.
Eagle, Houston. You are GO for DOI. Over.
Roger. GO for DOI. Do you have LOS and AOS times?
Roger. For you LOS at 101 28. AOS 102 16. Over.
And, Buzz, S band steerable update for you on the angles at AOS: 219 and yaw 30. Over.
Roger. That's in the flight plan. Thank you.
Houston, Columbia. How are all the systems looking?
Just wanted to get a systems check from you sometime prior to LOS.
Houston, Eagle. You can - Torquing angles NOUN 93 on four zeros and a 3 are minus 00292, plus 00289, minus 00094.
Roger. Copy. Stand by. Roger, Eagle. You can torque it. Over.
Columbia, Houston. Your systems are looking good going over the hill. Approximately 7 minutes to LOS.
Eagle, Houston. Place the BIOMED to Commander. Over.
Eagle, Houston. We've lost the high bit rate. Would you please select low bit rate? Over.
And, Eagle, on my Mark we'll have 12 minutes to ignition. Over.
Eagle, Houston. Stand by for my Mark.
Columbia/Eagle, Houston. Three minutes to LOS. Both looking good going over the hill.
Okay, state vector looks relatively good. ...
Columbia, Eagle. How do you read?
Very good. How do you read me?
Very good. If you are ready, give the mark and we'll go to B DATA. Over.
Okay, let's switch to B DATA now.
Mike, the burn's complete; it was on time - residuals are nulled, and AGS's free.
Roger. I'm ready to go back to VHF RANGING configuration. Be alright?
Roger. Let's go now to VHF RANGING.
Roger. That's just what we got, 7.6.
67 feet per second. Go ahead with the ...
Can't beat that. Okay, through with that?
Okay. And I'll pull the breakers - think we can ... roll.
Going to load the PDI plus 12, right?
Okay. I'm going to start pitching down to 125.
I have you right down ... 65 feet per second.
Okay, the camera is set. And ought to be ready to do the P52.
Not going to be much of a drift check.
It - it torques them late enough to ensure that - ... the drift check.
Sure seems like we're going the wrong way.
How much do we got to go to pick it up?
Got to go - oh, half the moon to go, I guess.
Okay. It's got us 152; it's 151; there's ..., okay? ...
Now we can let us take - let it take us there.
Yes, you'll have to roll over; well, I guess I might as well do that.
Where's your watch? Got your stopwatch?
And, one thing I'd appreciate if you could – see if you could - find the -
Yes. Which one do you want? I've got - -
That it? Where do you want it?
Trade you that for a piece of gum. There it is.
When do we have to get these? Alright, go on.
What do you mean by bringing - bringing CSM trash in here?
Well, that's stuff I had left over in my pocket.
No, I'm not AUTO; I'll be there in just a minute.
Well, we ought to proceed on that for a while.
These clocks you can't move like you can some. Let me try and get that clock set for PDI. ... 33 ...

Can't change this thing, once it gets going; like in the middle of a - -

No, that's the wrong circuit - that's ...
There's the sun in the COAS.
In the - I mean, in the reticle.
Alright, let me - let me do my rain dance with the DSKY here.
Now I need a VERB 76. I'm right on in pitch.
You want a VERB 76? Okay, you got it.
How are you doing - you going to be about ready to mark?
Say, how about you remembering the number that I read to you; don't have to write it down. Roll right just a little.
Oh, this cottonpicking - thought I was.
Okay. 134 17; KEY RELEASE; PROCEED. ... it should have been - 124 01. One more. Getting closer.
... - 13; KEY RELEASE; PROCEED. 4 13 - ... it should have been - closer yet.

Alright, let's go to - pitch to 180, 285, and zero.
Cottonpicker just won't stay - try it!
Well, wait until we lose that descent stage, man.
We'd better take - a - piece of tape; hold that down.
How about if you get the bottom in the – get the bottom underneath this cover? That help?
Well, it - it's still not; I've had it in there real good couple of times.
Your - hoses were tearing hell out of my board.
You got INVERTER 1 circuit breaker in, right?
Okay. I'm going to check INVERTER 1. INVERTER 2 is good; and INVERTER 1 is good, and we're on INVERTER.
Okay, get your AELD circuit breaker in and ABORT STAGE circuit breaker in.
AELD is in; ABORT STAGE is in.
Cycle the CWEA? No, we must have lost one.
Yes. That cottonpicker may be trouble.
Well, we'll have to tell them about that. I don't know when it - when it went out, because we didn't get any light that I saw, did you?
I think it's just a switch. I ... if it doesn't trigger a light -
Oh, we're in PULSE, and we're not commanding any firing - -
I don't know; that could have come under DOI, but I doubt it.

ENGINE STOP button is START, but it is going to be now.

- - ENABLE - ENABLE - THROTTLE in MINIMUM. Okay, in 35 minutes, we'll get the BAT feeds ON and - -

IN. Might look at the DPS.

Sounds like wind whipping around the trees.
Okay, we ready to go to P63?
Okay, get a - get a - Need to compare a TIG time. 09:50. That's right.

Okay, I'm going to get DESCENT QUANTITY, ON, ... ON.

Roger. I think I've got you on high gain now.
